drafts.rationale: Lightest passing design. Root stress 6PL/(b h^2) = 192 MPa vs 220.8 MPa allowable. REQ-006 worst case (2200 N, 24.5 mm) gives yield MS +0.004 and deflection 1.95 mm, so it passes with almost no margin. t/w = 1.67.
Alternative with more margin. Stress about 188 MPa. REQ-006 worst case gives yield MS +0.018 and deflection 2.42 mm. t/w = 0.83.
Stress about 133 MPa, yield MS +0.66. REQ-006 worst case gives yield MS +0.46 and deflection 1.12 mm. t/w = 2.00, exactly at the REQ-007 limit.
Highest-margin option of the four. Stress about 180 MPa. REQ-006 worst case gives yield MS +0.045 and deflection 2.97 mm. t/w = 0.41.

Lightest passing design found. Thickness 20 mm is stock. Nominal yield MS +0.85, ultimate MS +0.78, deflection 2.51 mm. Worst case (2200 N, 19.5 mm) gives deflection 2.98 mm, MS +0.60, so REQ-006 passes with little slack. t/w 1.69 passes REQ-007.

Same family as the lightest design with a little more width for margin. Nominal yield MS +0.88, ultimate MS +0.81, deflection 2.47 mm. Worst case gives deflection 2.93 mm, yield MS +0.62, so REQ-006 passes. t/w 1.67 passes REQ-007.

Stiffer option on a stock 25 mm plate. Nominal yield MS +2.06, ultimate MS +1.95, deflection 1.21 mm. Worst case gives deflection 1.42 mm, yield MS +1.67, so REQ-006 passes with large margin. t/w = 2.00 sits exactly at the REQ-007 limit and passes.

Wider, shallower section on a stock 16 mm plate with large stress margin. Nominal yield MS +1.40, ultimate MS +1.32, deflection 2.41 mm. Worst case gives deflection 2.92 mm, yield MS +1.05, so REQ-006 passes. t/w 0.67 passes REQ-007.

Lightest passing Steel 4130 section. Stress 300 MPa nominal, worst-case (2200 N, 19.5 mm) MS +0.002 so REQ-006 holds at the edge. Mass ~ 15x20 mm area x 150 mm x 7850 kg/m3. t/w 1.33 meets REQ-007. 20 mm is a stock thickness.

Thicker 25 mm plate with the narrowest width that keeps t/w <= 2. Nominal stress 230 MPa, worst-case MS +0.32, deflection 0.79 mm. Slightly heavier than the 15x20 option but with much more margin; t/w = 2.00 is exactly at the REQ-007 limit.
Mid-thickness alternative. Nominal stress 293 MPa, worst-case MS +0.013, deflection 1.62 mm. t/w 0.67. Heavier than the 25 mm option, so kept as a fallback.

Lead-suggested thin-plate region for reference. Nominal stress 284 MPa, worst-case MS +0.023, deflection 2.16 mm. Passes all requirements but is about 75% heavier than the 15x20 option, so it is not the minimum-mass choice.
Lightest feasible Al design. Passes REQ-001 to REQ-007 at nominal and worst case (worst-case yield MS +0.004, deflection 1.95 mm). Thin margin under REQ-006; Monte Carlo not run.
Passes all requirements. Worst-case yield MS +0.071, deflection 1.83 mm. Moderate margin for +10% load and -0.5 mm plate.
Chief engineer's directed width. Worst-case yield MS +0.205, deflection 1.63 mm, t/w 1.39. Passes all requirements with the most margin of the 25 mm options.
Alternate thickness. Passes all requirements. Worst-case yield MS +0.018, deflection 2.42 mm, t/w 0.83. Lower margin than the 25 mm options.

Lightest passing Ti design found. Nominal yield MS +0.85, ultimate MS +0.78, deflection 2.51 mm. Worst case (2200 N, 19.5 mm) gives yield MS +0.60 and deflection 2.98 mm, so REQ-006 passes. t/w = 1.69 passes REQ-007. 20 mm is stock. Deflection is the governing requirement.

Passes all requirements. Nominal yield MS +0.91, ultimate MS +0.84, deflection 2.43 mm. Worst case gives yield MS +0.65 and deflection 2.89 mm. t/w = 1.64. Slightly heavier than 11.8 x 20 but with more deflection margin.

Passes all requirements. Nominal yield MS +1.19, ultimate MS +1.11, deflection 2.12 mm. Worst case gives yield MS +0.89 and deflection 2.51 mm. t/w = 1.43. Mid-weight option with comfortable deflection margin.

Passes all requirements. Nominal yield MS +1.50, ultimate MS +1.41, deflection 1.85 mm. Worst case gives yield MS +1.16 and deflection 2.20 mm. t/w = 1.25. Most conservative of the four, at the highest mass.
Lightest Steel 4130 section that passes all requirements in check_design. Worst-case (2200 N, 19.5 mm) yield MS +0.002, so REQ-006 passes with almost no margin. Stock thickness 20 mm; t/w 1.33.
Passes all requirements. Worst-case yield MS +0.32 at 2200 N and 24.5 mm. t/w is exactly 2.00, at the REQ-007 limit. Stock thickness 25 mm.
Passes all requirements. Worst-case yield MS +0.37 and deflection 0.76 mm. t/w 1.92, inside REQ-007 with some margin. Stock thickness 25 mm.
Passes all requirements. Worst-case yield MS +0.42 and deflection 0.73 mm. t/w 1.85. Heaviest of the four, kept as a higher-margin fallback.

attacks.title: REQ-006 case: load +10% and plate 0.5 mm thinner
attacks.rationale: Combined check required by REQ-006. Stress_test: survives. Yield MS 0.595, ultimate MS 0.538, deflection 2.983 mm vs 3.0 mm limit. Passes, but the deflection margin is only 0.017 mm (0.6%).

attacks.title: Payload +25% (2500 N)
attacks.rationale: A heavier payload is a realistic change. Stress_test: fails. Deflection 3.142 mm exceeds 3.0 mm. Yield MS 0.477 and ultimate MS 0.423 remain positive, so stiffness governs, not strength.

attacks.title: Plate 1 mm thinner after machining (19 mm)
attacks.rationale: Machining or surface finishing can remove material. Stress_test: survives. Yield MS 0.666, ultimate MS 0.606, deflection 2.931 mm. Deflection scales with t^3, so thickness is the most sensitive dimension.

attacks.title: Arm 10 mm longer (160 mm) after layout change
attacks.rationale: A layout change lengthens the cantilever. Stress_test: fails. Deflection 3.050 mm exceeds 3.0 mm. Yield MS 0.731 and ultimate MS 0.668 remain positive. Deflection scales with L^3, so a 7% longer arm adds about 21% deflection.

attacks.title: Width 0.8 mm narrower (11.0 mm)
attacks.rationale: Width tolerance or machining loss reduces the section. Stress_test: survives. Yield MS 0.721, ultimate MS 0.659, deflection 2.696 mm. Margins drop but stay positive.

attacks.title: Fatigue at the clamp root
attacks.rationale: Cyclic bending at the clamp root, where stress is highest, is not modeled. The tool checks static strength only. Ti-6Al-4V notch sensitivity at the root is unknown, and no stress ratio or cycle count is given.

attacks.title: Stress concentrations at bolt holes or fillets
attacks.rationale: The model assumes a plain rectangular section. Holes or sharp corners at the clamp can raise local stress well above the nominal value and cut the margins substantially.

attacks.title: Dynamic or impact loading
attacks.rationale: The tool only scales a static load. Launch shock, vibration, or a drop event can produce load factors above the design value.

attacks.title: Off-axis loading, torsion, and lateral-torsional instability
attacks.rationale: The model assumes the load acts in the thickness direction. Any side load or twist adds torsion and lateral-torsional buckling risk, which REQ-007 (thickness/width <= 2) only partly covers.

attacks.title: Dimension and orientation ambiguity (11.8 x 20 mm)
attacks.rationale: The team's dimensions must be confirmed as width 11.8 mm and thickness 20 mm. 11.8 is not a stock thickness, so it cannot be the thickness. If the orientation is swapped, stiffness drops sharply.

attacks.title: Manufacturing tolerance bands and corrosion/galvanic coupling
attacks.rationale: The tool tests fixed losses, not tolerance bands or variation across the part. Ti in contact with Al or steel fasteners or structure can corrode galvanically, depending on the environment. Thermal changes also shift Ti-6Al-4V modulus and yield strength, which can alter deflection.

events.rule: a redesign needs a blocking finding
events.rationale: The selected 11.8 x 20 mm Ti-6Al-4V part passed the original envelope, but G-04 confirms that the 160 mm arm at 2500 N (the payload and arm change in the red team attack) pushes tip deflection to about 3.8 mm, over the REQ-003 limit of 3 mm, and the Monte Carlo (G-01) and breaking-point results (G-02, G-03) do not offset that deflection failure. The fix is within the envelope (width 10-60 mm and thickness/width <= 2), so another round of design changes can resolve it without escalation, and the risks in G-05 are carried as conditions.

events.summary: The bracket passes all six structural and factor-of-safety checks (S-01 through S-06) and the bare-metal finish, outgassing, stress corrosion, and buy-to-fly checks (M-02, M-03, M-04, F-01 through F-03), with the buy-to-fly ratio of 1.97 cited under F-02 as a cost driver. Open action items remain for allowables (M-01), dissimilar-metal galvanic control (M-05), fracture control classification (X-01), fatigue analysis (X-02), and the specialty metal, traceability, and supplier quality requirements (P-01 to P-03).
top_risks: Fatigue is not analyzed (X-02), so cyclic launch vibration loads are unverified despite the static margins passing (S-01 to S-03).
Design allowables are typical handbook values (M-01), so the margins rest on non-certified data until replaced with MMPDS A- or B-basis values for this alloy, temper, and thickness.
Specialty metal melt origin (P-01) under DFARS 252.225-7009 may constrain the supplier pool and schedule for the Ti-6Al-4V plate (F-01).

actions.action: Replace the typical values with MMPDS A- or B-basis allowables for Ti-6Al-4V in the specified temper and thickness, then rerun the margin calculations for S-01 to S-03.
Define the cyclic load cases, including launch vibration, and perform the fatigue analysis for the bracket.
Classify the part for fracture control (for example, non-fracture-critical) and record the rationale in the compliance file.
Specify fastener material and finish at the Ti-6Al-4V joint to prevent galvanic corrosion, per MIL-STD-889.
Confirm the melt origin of the specialty metal is the US or a qualifying country under DFARS 252.225-7009 before issuing the purchase order.
